page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-1xL40S is a GPU-accelerated virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9575F processor with 12 vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores at 2.0 GHz under a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.67 GB per core. Acceleration is driven by a single NVIDIA L40S GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, featuring 48 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression tests placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core performance and memory bandwidth read-only small block tests fall within the average range. Large block memory bandwidth read and write operations show strong performance in the top 25%. For artificial intelligence workloads, the NVIDIA L40S GPU delivers top-tier text generation speeds of 368.94 tokens per second for small 135M models, and strong text generation speeds of 36.32 tokens per second for medium 7B models.

This server offers a specialized hardware profile that balances high-capacity GPU resources with a shared CPU allocation. While the shared CPU model and lack of local storage present architectural tradeoffs, the high memory density and dedicated 48 GB VRAM make it a cost-efficient option for GPU-bound workloads rather than general-purpose compute. It is highly suited for large language model inference, image processing, text processing, and machine learning workloads that require significant VRAM but can tolerate shared CPU scheduling.
